clue.text: Those who beset others with dogs

definitions.meaning: people who harry or harass others, attacking them repeatedly
a breed of hound used for hunting hares

explanation.surface: Hunters who set their hounds on people.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass, so harassers are those who harry; the hound breed bred for hunting hares has the same name.

clue.text: US writer's abandoned Eastern lodge

indicators.note: the writer has dropped a letter, so one piece is taken out of the surname

parts.note: Harriet Beecher Stowe wrote Uncle Tom's Cabin

explanation.surface: An American author has left a Masonic lodge in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the writer has abandoned E. 'Lodge' is a verb here, to put away or store.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge something somewhere is to put it away or deposit it, as you would store luggage.

clue.text: Double perjury occupies judge

indicators.note: one piece takes up the space inside another, so it sits within it

parts.note: REF, short for referee, the judge of a match
perjury is telling a lie under oath

explanation.surface: Two counts of lying under oath keep the judge busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' looks like a quantity of perjury but is the definition: a stand-in or replacement.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a substitute who takes someone's place, as a relief worker takes over a shift.

clue.text: Clubs besieged by all the riff-raff

indicators.note: something besieged is surrounded, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the sum is the total, all of it
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Golf or social clubs are overrun by the rabble.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms are contemptuous names for the lowest, most worthless people in society.

clue.text: Item usually found on line, according to Bill Gates

definitions.text: Item usually found on line, according to Bill Gates

parts.words: Item usually found on line, according to Bill Gates
parts.note: a peg that holds washing on a line, dressed up as computer talk: 'on line' as online and PIN as a personal identification number

explanation.surface: The Microsoft founder describing something you find on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Gates suggests computing, and 'on line' reads as online; the line is really a washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg holds laundry on a washing line to dry.

clue.text: Incentive to stock endless holy books

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, having no end

parts.note: a shop that stocks goods carries them
OT is the Old Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: A reason for a shop to keep scripture in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward dangled to motivate someone, like the vegetable held before a donkey.

clue.text: Conservative CE involved with Latin hymn

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory in the Church of England takes up a Latin hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) suits the hymn picture but is just two letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a song or chant from scripture used in church services, so a kind of hymn.

clue.text: Rattle the manager?

definitions.meaning: Sir Simon Rattle, the British orchestra leader
one who conducts, that is directs or runs, affairs

explanation.surface: An instruction to unsettle the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Rattle leads orchestras with a baton; one who directs business is also said to conduct it.

clue.text: Nick's band

definitions.meaning: to nick is slang for arrest
a strip worn round the neck or round a pipe

explanation.surface: A belt belonging to someone called Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the two definitions; 'Nick' means arrest, as in police slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang uses one word for arresting someone, and the same word names a band encircling a neck.

clue.text: Horse tethered around Welsh tree

indicators.note: something tethered round another holds it inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat

explanation.surface: A horse tied up to a tree in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash is a tree with red berries, also called by this name.

clue.text: Innocent one gets time in jail

indicators.note: one pair of letters is placed inside the other word

parts.note: to immure is to shut up, imprison
A means one

explanation.surface: An innocent person is sent to prison for a term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jail' is a verb, IMMURE; A and T go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone childishly naive or unworldly is innocent in the sense of lacking experience.

clue.text: Fine stiff clues, cryptic, in Independent

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure and puzzling, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Hard cryptic clues appearing in the Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' looks like the newspaper but is the definition, meaning needing no one else.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can manage alone without outside help is independent.

clue.text: One with more than a passing interest in games

definitions.text: One with more than a passing interest in games

parts.words: One with more than a passing interest in games
parts.note: someone who plays soccer professionally, where passing the ball is part of the game

explanation.surface: A keen sports enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing interest' means casual, but here passing is kicking the ball to a team-mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional soccer player plays games for a living and passes the ball.

clue.text: Fiddler teases with instrument

parts.note: to card wool is to tease or comb it out
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A violinist mocks someone with a harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddler' seems a violinist, but means a cheat; to tease wool is to comb it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler is a swindler, and a cheat at cards is a cardsharp.

clue.text: Grades (including H) for films

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to grade is to sort, so grades are sorts

explanation.surface: Ratings for films include an H.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorts are brief films, often shown before the main feature.

clue.text: Strict line in public relations

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rope is a line, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A tough party line in the PR department.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and conventional, observing the rules exactly, in the sense of strict propriety.

clue.text: How a very short account might strike one

definitions.text: How a very short account might strike one

parts.words: How a very short account might strike one
parts.note: a bank balance that is tiny would cause shame, and a brief story might seem awkwardly brief

explanation.surface: A remark about a very brief story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' can be a story or a bank account; a low balance is shamefully short.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that strikes you as shamefully small makes you feel awkward.

clue.text: Dress — one to wear out, it's said

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: one is A, and to wear out is to tire

explanation.surface: A dress is something you tend to wear out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One to wear out' reads as A TIRE, which said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn, a formal word for garments or dress.

clue.text: State official presents college award, student's ultimate

parts.note: a diploma is awarded on completing a course

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An official is presented with a degree after a student's finals.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy representing a country abroad is an official of the state.

clue.text: Cash in money chest

parts.note: an ark is a chest, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Cash placed in a strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash' is the definition: the former German currency unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deutschmark was the German currency before the euro, so a form of cash.

clue.text: Receive grant

definitions.meaning: to let someone in, as to a club or hospital
to concede or acknowledge a point

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both letting a visitor in and conceding that something is true.

clue.text: Arch, one used to enter castle?

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: in chess a castle (rook) is one of the men
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A stone arch through which one enters a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' looks like a structure but means chief, as in arch-enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as a prefix means principal or chief, the same sense as principal.

clue.text: Be concerned with Queen's impetuous move

parts.note: to care is to be concerned
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Worrying about the Queen's rash action.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along headlong at speed, so a headlong rush.

clue.text: Pardon the delay

definitions.meaning: a postponement, especially of an execution

explanation.surface: Excuse me for being late.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution can be a full cancellation of punishment or just a postponement.
